headline: Performance-engineered software and LLM annotation speed biological data analysis
label: Scalable Bioinformatics Software Tools
summary: Recent preprints and publications pair fast Python, Rust, and JAX backends with zero-shot LLM annotation of genomic and sequencing data.
synthesis: The dominant thread is software engineered for throughput and accessibility in biological analysis, with LLMs increasingly applied to annotation. dna-parser uses a Python interface over a Rust backend to encode DNA and RNA sequences in parallel into numerical features for machine learning. BayesForge provides cross-platform Python, R, and Julia Bayesian inference with JAX backends, reported as up to 270x faster than Stan on large ecology networks. myLLannotator applies a 3B-parameter LLM zero-shot to microbial genome metadata, labeling over 18,000 genomes in about 2 hours. GPTBioInsightor and a microbiome metadata study evaluate LLM annotation of scRNA-seq cell types and sample biome origins, the latter validated on 1,000 curated samples. What is new is the pairing of performance engineering with zero-shot LLM annotation. The items span distinct domains and evidence types, and speed figures are as reported by the authors.
